verified.exploit_entry_point: supertest HTTP requests against the sync-server's exported Express handlers, backed by a real on-disk SQLite account DB seeded to represent a running multi-user/OpenID (or password) deployment; identical mechanism to the project's own test suite

co_present_vulns.proof_at_C: POST /simplefin/status and /pluggyai/status return 200 with no session token (no auth middleware on these routers)
a BASIC user reads/renames/reads-key of another user's file via /sync/get-user-file-info, /sync/update-user-filename, /sync/user-get-key (only a session check, no per-file access check)
POST /sync/upload-user-file with traversal in x-actual-file-id writes a blob outside the userFiles directory
a BASIC user calls /account/change-password (no admin check) then /account/login with loginMethod=password and receives the anonymous owner's ADMIN token
a BASIC user probes GET /secret/:name and learns whether a secret is configured (204/404); the write path has an admin check, the existence path does not
a disabled user's existing token still validates on /account/validate and /sync/list-user-files (session lookup never checks users.enabled)

dropped.reason: already fixed in 25.11.0, i.e. NOT present at C (26.2.0)

dropped.advisory: GHSA-m62c-5q34-f3cf / CVE-2026-57449 (CORS-proxy GitHub allowlist prefix bypass, CWE-200/284/863)
dropped.reason: present at C but not reproducible offline through the real entry point: the /cors-proxy route fetches its allowlist and proxies to api.github.com over the network, which is unavailable at run time

variants: missing-auth: SimpleFIN and Pluggy.ai /status AND /accounts unauthenticated

file-authz: cross-user read (get-user-file-info), rename (update-user-filename), key read (user-get-key), overwrite (upload-user-file over an existing file), reset (reset-user-file), download (download-user-file)
priv-esc: change-password (missing authz) + forced password login chain
secret-enum: GET /secret/:name existence disclosure to non-admin
session: disabled-user token accepted on /account/validate and /sync/list-user-files
services: none (sqlite account DB on local disk; no external services)
verified.project_tests_run: ran the project's own vitest suites src/app-account.test.js, src/app-sync.test.ts, src/app-admin.test.js at C in the image: 64 tests passed

patch_checks._why: 2026-10-16: reference fix + defensive hardening of util/paths.js (as MiMo did). The old test called getPathForUserFile itself and crashed on this; must pass.

2026-10-16 test repair: reference fix MINUS the per-file access check on upload-user-file (overwrite of an existing file), reset-user-file and download-user-file. Guards only the three originally-probed endpoints (get-user-file-info, update-user-filename, user-get-key), so it passes the old file-authz tests and all functional tests, but fails the new overwrite/reset/download cross-user probes. Proves those probes bite.

2026-10-16 test repair: reference fix but the SimpleFIN/Pluggy session check is attached only to the /status route instead of the whole router, leaving /accounts (and /transactions) unauthenticated. Passes the old /status missing-auth tests and the authed-status functional tests, but fails the new unauthenticated /accounts probes. Proves those probes bite.

notes: C = v26.2.0, the last release before the earliest included fix (26.2.1), chosen to maximise simultaneously-open advisories. 6 of 8 candidate advisories reproduced offline through HTTP; 2 dropped (one already fixed at C, one needs run-time network). Tests use the project's own harness shape (vitest + supertest against the exported handlers with a seeded sqlite account DB). Dependencies installed with npm in an isolated dir then moved into the package (monorepo root would otherwise pull every workspace); the single workspace dep @actual-app/web is stubbed (used only to locate the static web root).
